How to Start a WordPress Blog in Pakistan (2026): cPanel One-Click Install, Step by Step

By ZedgeHost Team · 22 November 2026 · 7 min read

Short answer: you need a domain name and WordPress hosting, then install WordPress in one click from cPanel. At ZedgeHost, WordPress hosting starts at Rs 1,499 per year and includes free SSL, free cPanel, weekly backups and free migration. The install takes a few minutes, and you can publish your first post the same day. Follow the steps below.

What you need before you start

A WordPress blog needs three things, and you can arrange all of them in one order. Get these ready first, and the install itself is the easy part.

  1. A domain name. This is your blog address. A .com costs Rs 2,999 for the first year and Rs 3,999 to renew, while a .pk costs Rs 4,999 for 2 years. Search for your name on the domain search page before you buy anything else.
  2. A WordPress hosting plan. This is where your blog lives. WordPress hosting from Rs 1,499 per year includes a one-click WordPress install, free SSL, free cPanel, weekly backups and free migration, so a new blog needs nothing else to start.
  3. An email address you actually read. WordPress sends password resets, comments and update notices to your admin email. Use a mailbox you check every day, not one you open once a month.

Install WordPress with the one-click installer in cPanel

Every WordPress plan at ZedgeHost includes a one-click WordPress install inside cPanel. You do not upload files, create a database or touch any code. The installer does all of that for you.

  1. Log in to cPanel. Use the cPanel login details from your hosting welcome email. If you ordered hosting and a domain together, both are already connected.
  2. Find the WordPress installer. Use the search box at the top of cPanel and type WordPress, then open the installer. It is listed as a one-click WordPress install.
  3. Choose your domain. Pick the domain from the list. Leave the directory field empty, so your blog opens on your main address, for example yourdomain.com, and not in a subfolder.
  4. Fill in the site details. Enter a site name, a short tagline, an admin username, a strong password and your admin email. Do not use admin as the username, because it is the first name attackers try.
  5. Click Install and wait. The installer creates the database and the WordPress files for you. It usually finishes in a minute or two.
  6. Log in at yourdomain.com/wp-admin. Use the admin username and password you just set. This is your WordPress dashboard, where you write posts, change the theme and manage comments.

If you cannot find the installer in your cPanel, contact 24/7 support and they will point you to it. For the full picture of what happens between ordering and activation, see how ordering works.

First settings to change after installing WordPress

WordPress works out of the box, but five quick settings make your blog cleaner and easier to find. Do them before you publish your first post.

  1. Set clean post links. Go to Settings, then Permalinks, and choose Post Name. Your posts will then have readable addresses like yourdomain.com/your-post-title.
  2. Set the timezone. Go to Settings, then General, and set the timezone to Karachi (UTC+5), so your post times match Pakistan time.
  3. Check the padlock. Visit your site with https in front and look for the padlock in the browser. Free SSL is included in every plan, so a new blog should already show it.
  4. Pick one simple theme. Choose a light, simple theme and stick with it for now. You can change the design any time without losing your posts.
  5. Write your first post. Go to Posts, then Add New, write a short introduction post, and publish it. A live post shows you the whole flow, from writing to reading it on your own domain.

5 mistakes beginners make with a WordPress blog

1. Using admin as the username

The username admin is the first one attackers try, and WordPress does not let you change a username later. Pick a different admin username at install time, and use a long password you do not reuse anywhere else.

2. Installing WordPress in a subfolder by accident

If you type blog into the directory field during install, your site opens at yourdomain.com/blog instead of yourdomain.com. Leave the directory field empty unless you deliberately want the blog in a folder. If you already installed it in a folder, reinstall it on the main address before you publish anything.

3. Publishing before checking SSL

Visitors trust the padlock, and browsers warn about sites without it. Check that your site loads with https before you share your first post. Free SSL is included in every plan, so if the padlock is missing, contact support instead of publishing anyway.

4. Skipping backups

A blog grows post by post, and losing it means losing months of work. Weekly backups are included in every plan, so confirm they are running and know how to restore from one. Never rely on a single copy of your posts.

5. Installing too many plugins at once

Each plugin adds load and another thing that can break or conflict. Start with only what you need, add one plugin at a time, and remove any you stop using. A new blog needs almost no plugins to publish its first posts.

After your first post: what next?

  1. Publish on a schedule you can keep. One good post a week beats ten rushed posts and then silence.
  2. Set up categories. A few clear categories help readers find related posts, and they keep your blog organised as it grows.
  3. Check your blog on a phone. Most readers in Pakistan will open your posts on a phone, so read your own post on one before you share it.
  4. Keep WordPress updated. Automatic WordPress core updates are included in every plan, so updates happen for you. Update your theme and plugins from the dashboard when WordPress tells you to.
